definition: In this context, an inpatient is a person admitted to a hospital or psychiatric ward for care and treatment, rather than being seen only during visits. Psychiatric inpatient hospitalisation means staying in hospital while receiving mental health care.

reasons: Adds an unsupported contrast (“rather than being seen only during visits”) that is not supported by the packet.
Uses a broader general definition of inpatient than the packet supplies; the source only supports psychiatric inpatient admissions/hospitalisation, not the full hospital/ward sense across settings.

The packet does not explicitly define what “inpatient” means (e.g., admitted for care/treatment rather than only attending visits). It only mentions “psychiatric inpatient admissions” and “hospitalisation,” without stating the general definition or the contrast with outpatient/visits.
The definition’s wording (“a person admitted to a hospital or psychiatric ward for care and treatment”) is not directly supported by the packet’s text.

The definition’s claim that psychiatric inpatient hospitalisation specifically means “staying in hospital while receiving mental health care” is not explicitly stated in the packet; the packet discusses consequences of psychiatric hospitalisation but does not define the term in those terms.
